title: dynamic-burst-credit-smoother-and-passive-reclaim-controller
author: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Tenants experiencing consecutive microbursts can cause large oscillations in their burst credit balance and aggressive reclaim which triggers backpressure and elevated latency tails. Existing burst accounting is reactive (hard drains / instant reclaim) and amplifies oscillation when multiple tenants alternate burst patterns. Goal: Introduce a controller that smooths per-tenant burst-credit accrual and reclaim signals using an EWMA + leaky-bucket hybrid, provide passive reclaim that prefers capacity backfill before hard drains, and expose observability hooks to measure credit oscillation and reclaim impact. The change is opt-in via feature flag `burst_smoother_v2` and is intended for Dedicated fleets and Private installs. What this PR does (high level): - Adds a new controller `BurstCreditSmootherController` in runtime/controller which maintains an EWMA-smoothed credit balance and a leaky reclaim window per tenant. - Implements passive reclaim logic: when the smoothed balance exceeds safe thresholds, the controller issues a reclaim with a configurable max rate instead of immediate hard drains; reclaim requests are eligible for backfill by idle capacity pools. - Introduces tenant-level safety caps and min-commit window to avoid starving long-running tenant workloads. - Adds feature flag gating, config knobs (smoothing_alpha, reclaim_rate_limit_qps, safety_cap_pct, min_commit_seconds) with sane defaults tuned from canary tests. - Adds and registers new telemetry metrics: `tenant_burst_credit_balance_gauge`, `tenant_burst_credit_smoothed_gauge`, `burst_reclaim_rate_counter`, `burst_reclaim_rate_histogram`, and `tenant_credit_oscillation_ratio` to quantify oscillation. - Updates Helm chart to include new RBAC and deployment manifest entries for the controller. - Adds unit tests and an e2e canary scenario (tests/e2e/burst_smoother_canary.yaml) used during staged rollout. Design notes: - Smoothing algorithm: EWMA on observed instantaneous balance with alpha default 0.15 (reduced from earlier 0.25 after reviewer feedback) to prioritize stability. Reclaim is enforced as a leaky token bucket where reclaim tokens are consumed at a bounded rate to avoid mass concurrent drains. - Backfill preference: reclaim requests are converted to low-priority backfill offers to warm pools and best-effort nodes; only if backfill is not accepted after a short window do we escalate to a hard drain. - Safety: tenants with active long-lived streams are exempted until min_commit_seconds elapses; safety_cap_pct provides a hard floor relative to contracted reservation. Rollout plan: 1) Feature flag rollout to 10% of Dedicated fleets (canary) with e2e scenario; monitor tenant_credit_oscillation_ratio and 95p latency. 2) If metrics stable after 48 hours, expand to 50% and run additional smoke tests. 3) Full rollout and mark feature flag default-on for new clusters in the next minor release. Testing and results: - Unit tests: new test coverage for controller logic, reclaim rate limiter, and edge cases (clock jumps, tenant churn). - Integration: initial integration run failed due to a race in config hot-reload (fixed in second commit). - Canary: synthetic microburst workload run on canary cluster shows reduced oscillation and latency improvements: 95th percentile tail latency down by ~8% and peak credit oscillation reduced by ~63% compared to baseline. CPU impact on controller pod ~+6% under sustained load. Backward compatibility & safety: - Opt-in via `burst_smoother_v2` feature flag. Default remains off for existing clusters until gradual rollout. - No user-facing API changes; config knobs are added to existing capacity/tenant config objects. - Breaking change: none. Related: ENG-2345 (autoscaler oscillation study), ENG-4048 (burst reclaim strategy doc), SUP-1123 (support ticket motivating urgent canary fix). Files of interest are summarized in changed_files.

release_notes: Introduce BurstCreditSmootherController (opt-in) to smooth tenant burst-credit oscillation and perform rate-limited passive reclaim with backfill preference. Adds observability metrics and new Helm flags. Expected to reduce latency tails during microbursts.
notes_perf: Canary reported 8% reduction in 95p latency under synthetic microburst and 63% reduction in measured credit oscillation. Controller CPU overhead ~6% at peak in Dedicated canary.
test_instructions: Enable feature flag `burst_smoother_v2` in charts/values.yaml, apply canary manifest in a dedicated test cluster, run tests/e2e/burst_smoother_canary.yaml, and monitor metrics tenant_credit_oscillation_ratio and tenant_burst_credit_smoothed_gauge for regressions.
